_about: What Elah and Montaigne may say, unasked, about a THING the pilot has: the ship they fly, their kit, a place they go, something they want or plan, something they like or dislike, the work they do. Edit the wording freely: every line here is said word for word, and a change is picked up the next time a line is chosen (no restart). Keep it valid JSON. {thing} is replaced by the name as the game data spells it (Cutlass Black, Grim HEX, mining); each line must have it exactly once. Under each relation the lines are grouped by what kind of thing it is, because the grammar differs: a ship, gun, armor or item takes 'the', a place, commodity, faction or maker does not, an activity is a plain lower-case word (it is given a capital when it opens the line). A group's key is the kinds it serves, separated by spaces. Add or remove lines as you like, but leave at least two in a group so the same one is not said twice running. If this file cannot be read, no such line is said at all.
_note: PROPOSALS, 2026-10-05. Every line in this file was written as a proposal for J to edit. J has NOT approved them yet. Change this note when he has. The feature is off until he has heard it (settings: fact_banter).
_rules: What a line here must keep to, whoever writes it. It is a small, light remark or question about the thing. It says nothing the fact does not support: a 'wants' or 'plans' line never talks as if the pilot has the thing, a 'goes_to' line never says why they go there, a 'dislikes' line never makes fun of the pilot. It never says or hints 'you told me', 'I remember you said', and never quotes. It never says that something is missing or has not happened. It is never a show of how much the companion remembers, and never a favour the pilot would owe for. Elah: one short sentence, no exclamation mark, no feeling of her own named. Montaigne: at most two sentences. Code checks every filled line against the chat gate and the attachment gate before it is said, and a line that fails is not said.
